review_notes:
I read the whole file. It has three kinds of new declarations. `cuspIntegral` is a public definition. `axisLimit` and the helper lemmas `hasDerivAt_line`, `exists_primitive`, `tendsto_limUnder_I_mul`, `tendsto_sub_vertical` and `integral_Ioi_eq_sub` are private. The rest are lemmas about `cuspIntegral`.

I looked for existing Mathlib or TauCeti notions of integrals between cusps, geodesic integrals, or primitives of holomorphic functions on ℍ. I found none. The only primitive construction nearby is `hasDerivAt_wedgeIntegral_upperHalfPlane` in TauCeti's `UpperHalfPlane/Primitive.lean`, and `exists_primitive` reuses it instead of competing with it. The private `axisLimit` is a `limUnder` along a specific axis. It is a proof-local device, not a competing concept. `cuspIntegral` is a well-defined cusp-to-cusp wrapper over `GL.geodesicIntegral` from `GeodesicIntegral.Basic`. It is a different object with its own invariance and additivity API, so I count it as a useful named specialisation. I did not open `GeodesicIntegral.Basic`, so I did not check whether it already contains an independent cusp-based definition. The grep over the TauCeti sources found no `cuspIntegral` competitor, but I did not search every file. I found no justified duplicate, so I abstain.
